name: How long does it take to construct an attached ADU?

mainEntity.name: How long does it take to construct an attached ADU?

acceptedAnswer.text: The timeline for constructing an attached ADU can vary depending on its size, complexity, and local permitting processes. Generally, the design and permitting phase can take anywhere from 3 to 6 months, sometimes longer in busy jurisdictions. Actual construction, once permits are secured, typically ranges from 4 to 9 months for a well-managed project. Factors like material availability, weather conditions, and the efficiency of the contractor can influence the overall duration. It's important to discuss a realistic timeline with your contractor during the planning stages.
acceptedAnswer.description: An attached ADU project can take 3-6 months for design and permitting, plus 4-9 months for construction, varying by complexity and local factors.
